## 1. System Architecture

### 1.1 Component Diagram

```
                              ┌─────────────────────────────┐
                              │   DNS (Cloudflare/registrar) │
                              │   *.bursary.elimux.ke  →     │
                              │   cname.vercel-dns.com       │
                              └──────────────┬───────────────┘
                                             │
                              ┌──────────────▼───────────────┐
                              │   Vercel (elimux-frontend)    │
                              │   Next.js App Router          │
                              │   - resolves tenant slug from │
                              │     Host header (edge)        │
                              │   - injects TenantProvider    │
                              │   - proxies /api/* to Railway │
                              └──────────────┬───────────────┘
                                             │ HTTPS (NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL)
                              ┌──────────────▼───────────────┐
                              │   Railway (elimux-backend)    │
                              │   Express, single service,    │
                              │   new routes under            │
                              │   /api/bursary/*               │
                              │   - resolveTenant middleware  │
                              │   - requireModule middleware  │
                              │   - existing adminAuth /      │
                              │     requireUser reused as-is  │
                              └──────────────┬───────────────┘
                                             │ service-role client
                              ┌──────────────▼───────────────┐
                              │   Supabase (project           │
                              │   ohlgjvenwekpbpkykutz)       │
                              │   - Postgres + RLS            │
                              │   - Storage (new bucket:      │
                              │     bursary-documents)        │
                              │   - Auth (shared auth.users)  │
                              └────────────────────────────────┘
```

This mirrors the existing ElimuX topology exactly (Vercel → Railway → Supabase, same three services as every other feature in the platform) — the Bursary Engine is a new set of tables and routes inside the *same* backend/database, not a separate deployment. `bursary.elimux.ke` is already added to the Vercel project and generating SSL per the instruction's Background — no new Vercel project is created.

### 1.2 Tenant Resolution Flow (subdomain → middleware → database query)

```
1. Request arrives: nairobi-county.bursary.elimux.ke/api/bursary/funds
2. Vercel/Railway receives the request; Host header = "nairobi-county.bursary.elimux.ke"
3. resolveTenant middleware (backend, mounted before all /api/bursary/* routes):
     a. If Host is one of the shared/unscoped hosts (app.elimux.ke, admin.elimux.ke,
        api.elimux.ke) → tenantId = null, continue (shared/global routes)
     b. Else, check tenant_domains for an exact match on Host with verified=true,
        status='active' → resolves custom-domain tenants (e.g. bursaries.nairobicounty.go.ke)
     c. Else, if Host has ≥3 dot-separated parts and the first isn't "www" → treat
        parts[0] as the tenant slug, look up tenants WHERE slug = parts[0] AND
        status = 'active'
     d. Else, fall back to the x-tenant-id header (API clients / mobile apps that
        can't rely on subdomain routing)
     e. If none resolve AND the path starts with /api/bursary/provider/ or
        /api/bursary/admin/ → 404 "Tender not found" (fail closed for tenant-only routes)
     f. Otherwise tenantId = null, continue (public discovery routes stay tenant-agnostic)
4. On success: req.tenant = { id, slug, name, status, activeModules, settings, branding },
   req.tenantId = tenant.id
5. Every downstream Supabase query filters .eq('tenant_id', req.tenantId) — see §5
6. RLS policies double-enforce the same scoping at the database layer (defense in depth,
   same pattern as every other ElimuX table — RLS is not the only gate, service-role
   backend queries bypass it, so the explicit .eq('tenant_id', ...) filter is what
   actually protects tenant isolation in the common case; RLS protects any future
   direct-from-browser Supabase access)
7. Response includes tenant branding data for frontend theming (see §7)
```

### 1.3 Module Activation Check Flow

```
1. Route handler declares its module requirement: requireModule('MOD_AI_ALLOCATION')
2. Middleware runs after resolveTenant (needs req.tenant already populated)
3. If req.tenant is undefined → 403 "Tenant context required" (route needs a tenant
   but resolveTenant fell through to the null-tenant branch)
4. If moduleId not in req.tenant.activeModules → 403 { error: "Module not activated",
   module: moduleId, upgrade_url: "https://elimux.ke/pricing" }
5. Else → next(), handler executes
6. activeModules is denormalized onto the tenants row (text[] column) for a single-query
   read on every request; bursary_module_configs holds the richer per-module settings
   and usage metrics, read only when a handler actually needs its settings (not on
   every gated request)
```

### 1.4 Request Lifecycle (full path)

```
DNS resolution (*.bursary.elimux.ke → Vercel edge)
  → Vercel Next.js middleware (edge): reads Host header, does NOT do the DB lookup
    itself (edge runtime, no direct Postgres access) — passes slug through as a
    request header (x-tenant-slug) so the page/API route doesn't re-parse Host
  → Next.js Server Component / Route Handler: either renders using cached branding
    (ISR) or proxies to Railway for anything requiring live tenant/module state
  → Railway Express app: CORS → helmet → (existing) admin/global middleware chain →
    resolveTenant → requireModule(...) if declared → route handler
  → Supabase: service-role client, .eq('tenant_id', ...) filtered query, RLS as
    second line of defense
  → Response bubbles back: Railway → Vercel (if proxied) → browser
```

## 2. Database Schema (SQL)

**Conventions matched to the live repo** (verified against `elimux-sql/`, not assumed): flat numbered `.sql` files (`elimux-sql/NN_description.sql`), no `migrations/` subfolder — highest existing file today is `43_drop_dangling_scholarship_provider_id.sql`, so the first Bursary Engine migration would be `44_...` when this blueprint moves to implementation (not created in this cycle — Risk constraint is docs-only). All tables use `gen_random_uuid()` for PKs and `timestamptz` for timestamps, matching every existing ElimuX table.

### 2.1 `tenants` (root of multi-tenancy)

```sql
CREATE TABLE tenants (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  slug varchar(63) UNIQUE NOT NULL, -- URL-safe: nairobi-county, safaricom-foundation
  name varchar NOT NULL,
  type varchar NOT NULL CHECK (type IN ('county','ngcdf','ward','ngo','csr','foundation','alumni','school','individual')),
  status varchar NOT NULL DEFAULT 'pending' CHECK (status IN ('pending','active','suspended','cancelled')),
  registration_number varchar, -- KRA PIN, NGO Board number, county gazette ref, etc.
  verification_status varchar NOT NULL DEFAULT 'pending' CHECK (verification_status IN ('pending','verified','suspended')),
  verification_documents jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '[]', -- [{type, url, uploaded_at}]
  contact jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}', -- {email, phone, address, county, sub_county, ward}
  active_modules text[] NOT NULL DEFAULT ARRAY['MOD_CORE','MOD_DISBURSE_MPESA','MOD_DISBURSE_EXTERNAL',
    'MOD_VERIFY_INSTITUTION','MOD_SCHOOL_MEDIATED','MOD_GUARDIAN_CONSENT','MOD_OFFLINE_QUEUE'], -- Phase 1 free-tier defaults, denormalized for single-query module gate reads
  module_settings jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}', -- per-module config, keyed by module_id
  billing_plan varchar NOT NULL DEFAULT 'free' CHECK (billing_plan IN ('free','essential','professional','enterprise')),
  billing_status varchar NOT NULL DEFAULT 'active' CHECK (billing_status IN ('active','past_due','cancelled')),
  budget_settings jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}', -- {annual_budget, per_student_cap, disbursement_methods[], fiscal_year_start}
  created_by uuid REFERENCES auth.users(id),
  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  updated_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

CREATE INDEX idx_tenants_slug ON tenants(slug);
CREATE INDEX idx_tenants_status ON tenants(status);

ALTER TABLE tenants ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;

CREATE POLICY "tenants_public_read_active" ON tenants
  FOR SELECT USING (status = 'active');

CREATE POLICY "tenants_admin_manage_own" ON tenants
  FOR ALL USING (
    EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM user_tenant_roles
            WHERE user_id = auth.uid() AND tenant_id = tenants.id AND role IN ('admin','super_admin'))
  );

CREATE POLICY "tenants_super_admin_all" ON tenants
  FOR ALL USING (
    EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM user_roles WHERE user_id = auth.uid() AND role = 'super_admin')
  );
-- NOTE: this policy reuses the EXISTING, real user_roles table (global admin flag,
-- no tenant_id column) for ElimuX-platform-level super admins — deliberately
-- distinct from the new, per-tenant user_tenant_roles table below. Do not
-- conflate the two: user_roles.role = 'super_admin' means "ElimuX platform
-- operator", user_tenant_roles.role = 'super_admin' (§2.4) means "owns this
-- one tenant, full control of its own data only".
```

### 2.2 `tenant_domains` (custom domain / CNAME support)

```sql
CREATE TABLE tenant_domains (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  tenant_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES tenants(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  domain varchar UNIQUE NOT NULL, -- e.g. bursaries.nairobicounty.go.ke
  type varchar NOT NULL CHECK (type IN ('subdomain','custom_domain')),
  verified boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false,
  verification_method varchar CHECK (verification_method IN ('dns_txt','cname','file_upload')),
  verification_token varchar,
  ssl_status varchar NOT NULL DEFAULT 'pending' CHECK (ssl_status IN ('pending','active','expired')),
  ssl_certificate_id varchar, -- Vercel domain-add response id
  status varchar NOT NULL DEFAULT 'pending' CHECK (status IN ('pending','active','failed','removed')),
  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  updated_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

CREATE INDEX idx_tenant_domains_domain ON tenant_domains(domain);
CREATE INDEX idx_tenant_domains_tenant ON tenant_domains(tenant_id);

ALTER TABLE tenant_domains ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;

CREATE POLICY "tenant_domains_admin_own" ON tenant_domains
  FOR ALL USING (
    EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM user_tenant_roles
            WHERE user_id = auth.uid() AND tenant_id = tenant_domains.tenant_id AND role IN ('admin','super_admin'))
  );
```

### 2.3 `tenant_branding` (white-label configuration)

```sql
CREATE TABLE tenant_branding (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  tenant_id uuid UNIQUE NOT NULL REFERENCES tenants(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  logo_url varchar,
  logo_dark_url varchar,
  primary_color varchar(7) DEFAULT '#0052CC', -- hex
  secondary_color varchar(7) DEFAULT '#FF6B00',
  accent_color varchar(7),
  font_family varchar DEFAULT 'system',
  favicon_url varchar,
  custom_css text,
  meta_title varchar,
  meta_description text,
  og_image_url varchar,
  language varchar NOT NULL DEFAULT 'en' CHECK (language IN ('en','sw','both')),
  support_phone varchar,
  support_email varchar,
  support_chat_enabled boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false,
  social_links jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}', -- {twitter, facebook, instagram, linkedin, whatsapp}
  legal_pages jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}', -- {privacy_policy_url, terms_url, cookie_policy_url, custom_legal_text}
  email_sender_name varchar,
  email_sender_domain varchar DEFAULT 'elimux.ke',
  sms_sender_id varchar(11), -- Safaricom-approved sender ID, hard 11-char cap
  public_dashboard_enabled boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false,
  show_recipient_names boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false,
  show_amounts boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT true,
  show_aggregate_only boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT true,
  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  updated_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

CREATE INDEX idx_tenant_branding_tenant ON tenant_branding(tenant_id);

ALTER TABLE tenant_branding ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;

CREATE POLICY "tenant_branding_public_read" ON tenant_branding
  FOR SELECT USING (true); -- branding is fetched by the public /api/tenants/:slug/branding route

CREATE POLICY "tenant_branding_admin_write" ON tenant_branding
  FOR INSERT WITH CHECK (
    EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM user_tenant_roles
            WHERE user_id = auth.uid() AND tenant_id = tenant_branding.tenant_id AND role IN ('admin','super_admin'))
  );
CREATE POLICY "tenant_branding_admin_update" ON tenant_branding
  FOR UPDATE USING (
    EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM user_tenant_roles
            WHERE user_id = auth.uid() AND tenant_id = tenant_branding.tenant_id AND role IN ('admin','super_admin'))
  );
```

### 2.4 `user_tenant_roles` (user ↔ tenant, per-tenant role)

```sql
CREATE TABLE user_tenant_roles (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  user_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES auth.users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  tenant_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES tenants(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  role varchar NOT NULL CHECK (role IN ('super_admin','admin','reviewer','viewer','finance','support')),
  permissions jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}',
  invited_by uuid REFERENCES auth.users(id),
  invited_at timestamptz,
  accepted_at timestamptz,
  status varchar NOT NULL DEFAULT 'pending' CHECK (status IN ('pending','active','suspended','removed')),
  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  updated_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  UNIQUE (user_id, tenant_id)
);

CREATE INDEX idx_user_tenant_roles_user ON user_tenant_roles(user_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_user_tenant_roles_tenant ON user_tenant_roles(tenant_id);

ALTER TABLE user_tenant_roles ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;

CREATE POLICY "user_tenant_roles_own" ON user_tenant_roles
  FOR SELECT USING (user_id = auth.uid());

CREATE POLICY "user_tenant_roles_tenant_admin" ON user_tenant_roles
  FOR ALL USING (
    EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM user_tenant_roles t2
            WHERE t2.user_id = auth.uid() AND t2.tenant_id = user_tenant_roles.tenant_id AND t2.role IN ('admin','super_admin'))
  );
-- NOTE: self-referencing policy — matches the same pattern the existing
-- scholarship_providers admin policies use (subquery against the same table),
-- Postgres RLS supports this safely because the subquery re-evaluates per row.
```

*A user's global platform role continues to live in the existing `user_roles` table (`student|partner|advertiser|institution|admin|super_admin`, no `tenant_id`) — unrelated and untouched. A user can simultaneously be `admin` of Nairobi County (`user_tenant_roles`), `reviewer` of Safaricom Foundation (`user_tenant_roles`), and have no row in `user_roles` at all (an ordinary student on the existing scholarship platform).*

### 2.5 `bursary_providers` (extends tenants)

```sql
CREATE TABLE bursary_providers (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY REFERENCES tenants(id) ON DELETE CASCADE, -- 1:1 with tenants, PK = tenants.id
  tenant_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES tenants(id) ON DELETE CASCADE, -- denormalized, always equals id
  type varchar NOT NULL CHECK (type IN ('county','ngcdf','ward','ngo','csr','foundation','alumni','school')),
  registration_number varchar,
  verification_status varchar NOT NULL DEFAULT 'pending' CHECK (verification_status IN ('pending','verified','suspended')),
  verification_documents jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '[]',
  contact jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}',
  admin_users uuid[] NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}',
  active_modules text[] NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}', -- kept in sync with tenants.active_modules by application code; tenants row is source of truth for the module-gate middleware
  module_settings jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}',
  budget_settings jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}',
  branding_id uuid REFERENCES tenant_branding(id),
  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  updated_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  CHECK (id = tenant_id)
);

CREATE INDEX idx_bursary_providers_tenant ON bursary_providers(tenant_id);

ALTER TABLE bursary_providers ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;

CREATE POLICY "bursary_providers_public_read_verified" ON bursary_providers
  FOR SELECT USING (verification_status = 'verified');

CREATE POLICY "bursary_providers_admin_own" ON bursary_providers
  FOR ALL USING (
    EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM user_tenant_roles
            WHERE user_id = auth.uid() AND tenant_id = bursary_providers.tenant_id AND role IN ('admin','super_admin'))
  );
```

**Naming-collision flag:** an unrelated table `scholarship_providers` already exists in production (verified/is_partner/claimed_by columns, powers the *scholarship* partner-gate feature shipped in an earlier cycle). `bursary_providers` is a **new, separate** table for the Bursary Engine — do not merge or alias these; they serve different products (discovery-only scholarship listings vs. tenant-owning bursary funders) even though the names are one word apart.

### 2.6 `bursary_funds`

```sql
CREATE TABLE bursary_funds (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  tenant_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES tenants(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  provider_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES bursary_providers(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  name varchar NOT NULL,
  description text,
  fund_type varchar NOT NULL CHECK (fund_type IN ('open','targeted','emergency','renewal')),
  status varchar NOT NULL DEFAULT 'draft' CHECK (status IN ('draft','open','closed','disbursing','completed','cancelled')),
  budget jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}', -- {total, committed, disbursed, remaining, currency}
  eligibility_rules jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}', -- courses[], institutions[], counties[], min_kcse_grade, max_household_income, priority_categories[], gender_target, disability_quota, rural_urban_ratio
  required_documents jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '[]', -- [{type, required, ai_verifiable, condition?}]
  application_window jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}', -- {opens_at, deadline, notification_date}
  disbursement_rules jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}', -- {methods[], staged, stages[], min_amount, max_amount, currency}
  allocation_rules jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}', -- {scoring_weights, equity_constraints, ai_optimization_enabled, human_override_required}
  renewal_rules jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}', -- {renewable, max_renewals, min_gpa, require_mid_term_report, auto_renewal_threshold}
  fraud_detection_settings jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}', -- {duplicate_identity_check, document_recycling_check, velocity_check, income_consistency_check, manual_review_threshold}
  created_by uuid REFERENCES auth.users(id),
  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  updated_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

CREATE INDEX idx_bursary_funds_tenant ON bursary_funds(tenant_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_bursary_funds_provider ON bursary_funds(provider_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_bursary_funds_status ON bursary_funds(status) WHERE status = 'open';

ALTER TABLE bursary_funds ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;

-- Matches v2 blueprint Appendix A verbatim (already tenant-correct in source)
CREATE POLICY "bursary_funds_public_read_open" ON bursary_funds
  FOR SELECT USING (
    status = 'open'
    AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM tenants WHERE id = bursary_funds.tenant_id AND status = 'active')
  );

CREATE POLICY "bursary_funds_tenant_admin_manage" ON bursary_funds
  FOR ALL USING (
    tenant_id = current_setting('app.current_tenant_id', true)::uuid
    AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM user_tenant_roles
                WHERE user_id = auth.uid() AND tenant_id = bursary_funds.tenant_id AND role IN ('admin','super_admin'))
  );

CREATE POLICY "bursary_funds_applicant_read_applied" ON bursary_funds
  FOR SELECT USING (
    EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM bursary_applications
            WHERE fund_id = bursary_funds.id AND applicant_id IN (
              SELECT id FROM bursary_applicants WHERE user_id = auth.uid()
            ))
  );
```

### 2.7 `bursary_applicants`

```sql
CREATE TABLE bursary_applicants (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  tenant_id uuid REFERENCES tenants(id), -- nullable: self-service applicants aren't tied to a school tenant
  user_id uuid REFERENCES auth.users(id), -- nullable for school-mediated applicants without their own account yet
  application_type varchar NOT NULL CHECK (application_type IN ('self','school_mediated','guardian_assisted')),
  school_id uuid REFERENCES institutions(id), -- reuses EXISTING institutions table, not a new one
  teacher_id uuid REFERENCES auth.users(id),
  personal_info jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}', -- full_name, date_of_birth, gender, national_id (hashed), phone, email, guardian_phone/email, guardian_consent_status, guardian_consent_otp (hashed), language_preference
  academic_info jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}', -- current_institution_id, course_name/code, study_level, year_of_study, kcse_grade/index_number/year, current_gpa, previous_transcripts[]
  residence_info jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}', -- county, sub_county, ward, village, constituency, rural_urban, years_in_residence
  household_info jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}', -- household_size, dependents, income_sources[], total_monthly_income, income_verification_status, primary_caregiver, caregiver_employment/phone, orphan_status, disability_status
  vulnerability_index jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}', -- {raw_score, components{...}, calculated_at, data_sources[]}
  application_status varchar NOT NULL DEFAULT 'draft' CHECK (application_status IN
    ('draft','submitted','document_check','institution_verify','govt_verify','provider_review',
     'approved','rejected','waitlisted','disbursed','appealed')),
  fraud_score numeric NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (fraud_score BETWEEN 0 AND 100),
  fraud_flags jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '[]',
  eligibility_score numeric CHECK (eligibility_score BETWEEN 0 AND 1000),
  eligibility_breakdown jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}',
  appeal_status varchar NOT NULL DEFAULT 'none' CHECK (appeal_status IN ('none','pending','resolved')),
  appeal_reason text,
  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  updated_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

CREATE INDEX idx_bursary_applicants_user ON bursary_applicants(user_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_bursary_applicants_tenant ON bursary_applicants(tenant_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_bursary_applicants_school ON bursary_applicants(school_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_bursary_applicants_status ON bursary_applicants(application_status);

ALTER TABLE bursary_applicants ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;

CREATE POLICY "bursary_applicants_own" ON bursary_applicants
  FOR ALL USING (user_id = auth.uid());

CREATE POLICY "bursary_applicants_school_admin" ON bursary_applicants
  FOR ALL USING (
    application_type = 'school_mediated'
    AND teacher_id = auth.uid()
  );

CREATE POLICY "bursary_applicants_provider_review" ON bursary_applicants
  FOR SELECT USING (
    EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM bursary_applications a
            JOIN user_tenant_roles r ON r.tenant_id = a.tenant_id
            WHERE a.applicant_id = bursary_applicants.id AND r.user_id = auth.uid() AND r.role IN ('admin','reviewer','super_admin'))
  );
```

*The `document_id`-level forensics detail from the source blueprint's `applicant.documents` JSON array is normalized into its own `bursary_documents` table below — Task 2 explicitly lists `bursary_documents` as a separate required table, so per-document forensics results live there, not nested JSON on the applicant.*

### 2.8 `bursary_applications`

```sql
CREATE TABLE bursary_applications (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  applicant_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES bursary_applicants(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  fund_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES bursary_funds(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  provider_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES bursary_providers(id),
  tenant_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES tenants(id),
  status varchar NOT NULL DEFAULT 'draft', -- mirrors bursary_applicants.application_status, kept in sync by application code on transition
  submission_data jsonb, -- snapshot of applicant fields at submit time (immutable once set)
  eligibility_score numeric CHECK (eligibility_score BETWEEN 0 AND 1000),
  eligibility_breakdown jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}',
  fraud_score numeric NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (fraud_score BETWEEN 0 AND 100),
  fraud_flags jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '[]',
  document_status jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}', -- {total_documents, verified, rejected, pending, overall_risk} — denormalized rollup of bursary_documents rows
  institution_verification jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}', -- {status, verified_by, verified_at, digital_signature, notes, student_confirmed_enrolled}
  government_verification jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}', -- {status, verified_by, verified_at, residence_confirmed, household_assessment, notes}
  provider_decision jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}', -- {status, decided_by, decided_at, amount_awarded, award_type, conditions[], reason, ai_suggestion_followed}
  allocation_data jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}', -- {ai_suggested_amount, ai_suggested_rank, human_override, override_reason, equity_adjustment}
  disbursement_plan jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '[]', -- [{stage, percent, amount, trigger, status, disbursed_at, transaction_reference}]
  appeal_data jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}',
  audit_trail jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '[]', -- append-only state-change log
  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  updated_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  UNIQUE (applicant_id, fund_id) -- one fund per student, per v2 §Appendix A allocation constraint 9
);

CREATE INDEX idx_bursary_applications_applicant ON bursary_applications(applicant_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_bursary_applications_fund ON bursary_applications(fund_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_bursary_applications_tenant ON bursary_applications(tenant_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_bursary_applications_status ON bursary_applications(status);

ALTER TABLE bursary_applications ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;

CREATE POLICY "bursary_applications_applicant_own" ON bursary_applications
  FOR SELECT USING (
    EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM bursary_applicants WHERE id = bursary_applications.applicant_id AND user_id = auth.uid())
  );

CREATE POLICY "bursary_applications_provider_admin" ON bursary_applications
  FOR ALL USING (
    EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM user_tenant_roles
            WHERE user_id = auth.uid() AND tenant_id = bursary_applications.tenant_id AND role IN ('admin','reviewer','super_admin'))
  );

CREATE POLICY "bursary_applications_institution_admin" ON bursary_applications
  FOR SELECT USING (
    EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM bursary_applicants ba
            WHERE ba.id = bursary_applications.applicant_id AND ba.teacher_id = auth.uid())
  );
```

### 2.9 `bursary_documents` (uploaded documents with forensics)

```sql
CREATE TABLE bursary_documents (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  applicant_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES bursary_applicants(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  application_id uuid REFERENCES bursary_applications(id) ON DELETE CASCADE, -- nullable: documents can be uploaded to a profile before an application exists
  tenant_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES tenants(id),
  document_type varchar NOT NULL, -- 'national_id' | 'admission_letter' | 'kcse_certificate' | 'fee_structure' | 'recommendation_letter' | 'guardian_consent' | 'disability_certificate' | 'chief_letter' | ...
  file_url varchar NOT NULL, -- Supabase Storage path in the bursary-documents bucket
  file_hash varchar NOT NULL, -- SHA-256, exact-duplicate detection
  perceptual_hash varchar, -- pHash, near-duplicate / recycled-document detection
  upload_method varchar NOT NULL CHECK (upload_method IN ('online','offline_queue','school_upload')),
  forensics_result jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}', -- {risk_score, tamper_flags[], format_valid, cross_ref_status, ai_confidence, stage_results{...}, heatmap_url}
  risk_score numeric CHECK (risk_score BETWEEN 0 AND 100), -- denormalized from forensics_result for fast filtering/sorting
  status varchar NOT NULL DEFAULT 'pending' CHECK (status IN ('pending','verified','rejected','expired')),
  uploaded_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  reviewed_at timestamptz,
  reviewed_by uuid REFERENCES auth.users(id)
);

CREATE INDEX idx_bursary_documents_applicant ON bursary_documents(applicant_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_bursary_documents_application ON bursary_documents(application_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_bursary_documents_perceptual_hash ON bursary_documents(perceptual_hash); -- duplicate-detection lookups
CREATE INDEX idx_bursary_documents_file_hash ON bursary_documents(file_hash);

ALTER TABLE bursary_documents ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;

CREATE POLICY "bursary_documents_own" ON bursary_documents
  FOR ALL USING (
    EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM bursary_applicants WHERE id = bursary_documents.applicant_id AND user_id = auth.uid())
  );

CREATE POLICY "bursary_documents_provider_review" ON bursary_documents
  FOR SELECT USING (
    EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM user_tenant_roles
            WHERE user_id = auth.uid() AND tenant_id = bursary_documents.tenant_id AND role IN ('admin','reviewer','super_admin'))
  );
```

### 2.10 `bursary_disbursements` (immutable ledger)

```sql
CREATE TABLE bursary_disbursements (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  application_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES bursary_applications(id),
  provider_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES bursary_providers(id),
  applicant_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES bursary_applicants(id),
  tenant_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES tenants(id),
  amount numeric NOT NULL CHECK (amount > 0),
  currency varchar(3) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'KES',
  method varchar NOT NULL CHECK (method IN ('mpesa','bank_transfer','external','direct_institution')),
  status varchar NOT NULL DEFAULT 'pending' CHECK (status IN ('pending','initiated','completed','failed','reversed')),
  transaction_details jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}', -- shape varies by method: mpesa{checkout_request_id,...} | bank{account_number,...} | external{payment_date,...} | direct_institution{institution_id,...}
  stage int NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,
  term int,
  academic_year varchar,
  ledger_hash varchar NOT NULL, -- SHA-256(previous_hash || row data) — computed by application code before insert, never by a DB trigger, so the hash covers exactly what the app sent
  previous_hash varchar, -- null only for a tenant's first-ever disbursement row
  public_visibility varchar NOT NULL DEFAULT 'aggregate_only' CHECK (public_visibility IN ('full','aggregate_only','anonymous','private')),
  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
  -- Deliberately no updated_at: this table is INSERT-only by design (immutable ledger).
  -- Corrections happen via a new compensating row (status='reversed' + a fresh entry), never UPDATE.
);

CREATE INDEX idx_bursary_disbursements_application ON bursary_disbursements(application_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_bursary_disbursements_tenant ON bursary_disbursements(tenant_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_bursary_disbursements_applicant ON bursary_disbursements(applicant_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_bursary_disbursements_status ON bursary_disbursements(status);

ALTER TABLE bursary_disbursements ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;

CREATE POLICY "bursary_disbursements_provider_admin" ON bursary_disbursements
  FOR ALL USING (
    EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM user_tenant_roles
            WHERE user_id = auth.uid() AND tenant_id = bursary_disbursements.tenant_id AND role IN ('admin','finance','super_admin'))
  );

CREATE POLICY "bursary_disbursements_public_read" ON bursary_disbursements
  FOR SELECT USING (public_visibility != 'private');

-- No UPDATE/DELETE policy granted to any role including admins — enforces
-- immutability at the RLS layer, not just by application convention. A
-- genuine correction requires a new row referencing this one, never a mutation.
```

### 2.11 `bursary_fraud_registry` (cross-tenant, hashed identifiers)

```sql
CREATE TABLE bursary_fraud_registry (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  fraud_type varchar NOT NULL CHECK (fraud_type IN
    ('duplicate_identity','ghost_student','income_fraud','document_recycling',
     'velocity_abuse','social_collusion','institution_collusion','provider_collusion')),
  severity varchar NOT NULL CHECK (severity IN ('low','medium','high','critical')),
  identifiers jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}', -- {national_id_hash, phone_hash, email_hash, device_fingerprint (all salted SHA-256), ip_address_range} — NEVER raw PII, see §9
  evidence jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}', -- redacted case detail
  affected_applications uuid[] NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}',
  affected_providers uuid[] NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}', -- intentionally cross-tenant: this is the one table where a row can reference multiple tenants' provider ids at once
  status varchar NOT NULL DEFAULT 'active' CHECK (status IN ('active','investigating','confirmed','dismissed','appealed')),
  action_taken varchar NOT NULL DEFAULT 'none' CHECK (action_taken IN
    ('none','application_blocked','applicant_banned','institution_flagged','provider_notified')),
  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  updated_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

CREATE INDEX idx_fraud_registry_identifiers ON bursary_fraud_registry USING gin (identifiers);
CREATE INDEX idx_fraud_registry_status ON bursary_fraud_registry(status);

ALTER TABLE bursary_fraud_registry ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;

CREATE POLICY "bursary_fraud_registry_super_admin_only" ON bursary_fraud_registry
  FOR ALL USING (
    EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM user_roles WHERE user_id = auth.uid() AND role = 'super_admin')
  );
-- Deliberately the ONLY table in this schema with zero tenant-scoped access —
-- per v1 §12.4, registry access is super-admin only regardless of tenant,
-- because it is the cross-tenant fraud defense (a provider must never be
-- able to read which OTHER providers a hashed identifier touched).
```

**Flag (open question, not decided unilaterally):** the source v2 blueprint specs `stripe_customer_id`/`stripe_subscription_id`. Live ElimuX's actual subscription billing (`elimux-backend/src/routes/payments.ts`, `subscribers`/`subscriptions` tables) runs on **Paystack**, not Stripe — a `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` env var exists but there's no evidence it's wired to any live route, while Paystack merchant approval is a known open item (separate from this cycle). Renamed the columns `paystack_customer_code`/`paystack_subscription_code` to match the platform's actual processor rather than silently keeping unused Stripe fields — flagging this for founder/Kimi confirmation rather than assuming, since it's a real product decision (does Bursary Engine billing reuse the existing Paystack subscriber flow, or need its own processor integration?).

```sql
CREATE TABLE bursary_mpesa_transactions (

CREATE POLICY "bursary_mpesa_provider_admin" ON bursary_mpesa_transactions
  FOR ALL USING (
    EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM user_tenant_roles
            WHERE user_id = auth.uid() AND tenant_id = bursary_mpesa_transactions.tenant_id AND role IN ('admin','finance','super_admin'))
  );
```

**Naming deviation from Task 2's literal table name (`mpesa_transactions`), flagged deliberately:** Cycle 013's KIMI DESIGN instruction (still **BLOCKED**, unshipped, per `docs/archive/bridge-013.md`) already proposed a table literally named `mpesa_transactions` for the *scholarship-subscription* M-Pesa flow, and that decision is still pending founder/Kimi sign-off. Using the same name here for a *different* (bursary disbursement) M-Pesa flow would create exactly the kind of two-tables-one-name collision this codebase has hit before (`scholarship_provider_id` vs `provider_id`, `adminAuth` vs `adminMiddleware`). Renamed to `bursary_mpesa_transactions` to keep the two proposals non-colliding regardless of which order they eventually ship in. Also note: live Railway env vars today have `MPESA_CONSUMER_KEY`/`MPESA_CONSUMER_SECRET` set, but `MPESA_PASSKEY`/`MPESA_SHORTCODE`/`MPESA_CALLBACK_URL` were confirmed **unset** as of Cycle 013's investigation — same blocker applies to Bursary Engine M-Pesa disbursement, see §12.4.

### 2.15 `bursary_audit_logs` — bonus table, added beyond Task 2's literal 14-table list

Task 2 lists 14 named tables, but Task 3's acceptance criterion says "every table from the v2 blueprint has a CREATE TABLE statement" — and the v2 source (§4.6) explicitly lists `bursary_audit_logs` as one of the tables "requiring tenant_id." Section 9 (Security & Compliance) also requires an audit-logging strategy, which is hard to make concrete without a backing table. Added here as a deliberate scope addition to resolve that inconsistency between Task 2 and Task 3, flagged rather than silently expanded.

```sql
CREATE TABLE bursary_audit_logs (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  tenant_id uuid REFERENCES tenants(id), -- nullable: platform-level events (e.g. tenant creation itself) have no tenant yet
  actor_id uuid REFERENCES auth.users(id),
  actor_role varchar, -- snapshot of the role at action time, since user_tenant_roles can change later
  action varchar NOT NULL, -- e.g. 'application.approved', 'disbursement.initiated', 'module.activated'
  entity_type varchar NOT NULL, -- 'bursary_applications' | 'bursary_disbursements' | 'tenants' | ...
  entity_id uuid,
  before_state jsonb,
  after_state jsonb,
  ip_address varchar, -- read from x-forwarded-for (Railway strips real client IP on req.ip — same fix already applied elsewhere in this backend, see reviews.ts)
  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

CREATE INDEX idx_bursary_audit_logs_tenant ON bursary_audit_logs(tenant_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_bursary_audit_logs_entity ON bursary_audit_logs(entity_type, entity_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_bursary_audit_logs_actor ON bursary_audit_logs(actor_id);

ALTER TABLE bursary_audit_logs ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;

CREATE POLICY "bursary_audit_logs_tenant_admin_read" ON bursary_audit_logs
  FOR SELECT USING (
    EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM user_tenant_roles
            WHERE user_id = auth.uid() AND tenant_id = bursary_audit_logs.tenant_id AND role IN ('admin','super_admin'))
  );
CREATE POLICY "bursary_audit_logs_super_admin" ON bursary_audit_logs
  FOR ALL USING (
    EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM user_roles WHERE user_id = auth.uid() AND role = 'super_admin')
  );
-- INSERT is service-role only in practice (backend writes every row); no
-- authenticated-user INSERT policy is granted, matching an append-only log.
```

### 2.16 Existing tables that need `tenant_id` added (not new tables — `ALTER TABLE`)

Per v2 §4.6, these already-live tables are named as needing tenant-scoping if/when the Bursary Engine reuses them. Each needs its own migration when implementation starts, not a `CREATE TABLE`:

| Table | Change | Why nullable |
|---|---|---|
| `payments` (Paystack, `elimux-backend/src/routes/payments.ts`) | `ALTER TABLE payments ADD COLUMN tenant_id uuid REFERENCES tenants(id)` | Existing rows (scholarship subscriptions) predate tenants and have no tenant — must stay nullable, not backfillable |
| `scholarship_messages` | `ALTER TABLE scholarship_messages ADD COLUMN tenant_id uuid REFERENCES tenants(id)` | Only relevant if bursary provider↔applicant messaging reuses this table instead of a bursary-specific one — **flagged as an open design question**, not decided here: the source blueprint mentions this only as "(if used for bursary communication)," itself conditional |

`institutions` and `countries` remain global reference tables (no `tenant_id`) — every school/university and every country is visible to every tenant, matching how they already work for the scholarship platform. `users`/`auth.users` and the existing `user_roles` table are explicitly cross-tenant per v2 §4.6 and are **not** altered.

---

## 3. Backend API Specification

All routes below are mounted under `/api/bursary/*` on the existing single Railway service (no new deployment) — matching the instruction's Section 8 requirement. `resolveTenant` runs ahead of every route in this list (mounted once, at the `/api/bursary` router level, matching how `helmet()`/`cors()` are already mounted ahead of all existing routers in `index.ts`). "Module Check" values reference the module registry in §6.1.

Auth values: **Public** = no auth header required. **Student** = existing `requireUser` middleware (`req.userId`/`req.userEmail`, from `middleware/user-auth.ts` — reused as-is, not reimplemented). **Tenant Admin** = new `requireTenantRole('admin','super_admin')` (checks `user_tenant_roles` for `req.tenantId`). **Institution Admin** = `requireTenantRole` scoped to a school-type tenant, or the existing `institutionAuth` middleware if the school is acting through its existing institution-portal login rather than a bursary tenant login (flagged as a design choice for Kimi — the source blueprint assumes a fresh institution-admin concept; ElimuX already has one via `institution-auth.ts`, reuse is the leaner option). **Govt Admin** = `requireTenantRole` scoped to a `ward`/`county`/`ngcdf` tenant type. **Super Admin** = existing `adminAuth` (unified onto this single function since Cycle 005 — reused, not reimplemented).

### 3.1 Tenant Management

| Method | Path | Auth | Module Check | Request Body | Response |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/tenants/:slug/branding` | Public | None | — | `TenantBranding` (§2.3 columns, camelCased) |
| GET | `/api/tenants/:slug/modules` | Public | None | — | `{ activeModules: string[] }` |
| GET | `/api/tenants/:slug/public` | Public | None | — | `{ name, type, verified, description }` |
| GET | `/api/tenants/:slug/stats` | Public | None | — | `{ totalDisbursed, studentsHelped, currency }` (from `bursary_disbursements` where `public_visibility != 'private'`) |
| POST | `/api/tenants` | Super Admin | None | `{ slug, name, type, registrationNumber, contact }` | `201 { tenant }` |
| PATCH | `/api/tenants/:id` | Tenant Admin | None | Partial `tenants` fields | `200 { tenant }` |
| POST | `/api/tenants/:id/domains` | Tenant Admin | MOD_CUSTOM_DOMAIN | `{ domain }` | `201 { tenant_domain, dns_instructions }` |
| POST | `/api/tenants/:id/domains/:domainId/verify` | Tenant Admin | MOD_CUSTOM_DOMAIN | — | `200 { verified: boolean }` |
| POST | `/api/tenants/:id/branding` | Tenant Admin | None | `TenantBranding` fields | `200 { branding }` |
| POST | `/api/tenants/:id/modules` | Tenant Admin | None | `{ modules: string[], settings: object }` | `200 { activated, billingChange, effectiveDate }` |
| GET | `/api/tenants/:id/users` | Tenant Admin | None | — | `{ users: UserTenantRole[] }` |
| POST | `/api/tenants/:id/users` | Tenant Admin | None | `{ email, role }` | `201 { invitation }` |
| DELETE | `/api/tenants/:id/users/:userId` | Tenant Admin | None | — | `204` |

### 3.2 Provider Onboarding

| Method | Path | Auth | Module Check | Request Body | Response |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| POST | `/api/bursary/providers/register` | Public | None | `{ orgName, type, registrationNumber, contact, adminUser: {name,email,phone} }` | `201 { tenant, provider, loginInstructions }` — creates `tenants` + `bursary_providers` rows atomically, defaults `active_modules` to the Phase-1 free tier list |
| POST | `/api/bursary/providers/:id/verify` | Super Admin | None | `{ verificationStatus, notes }` | `200 { provider }` |
| GET | `/api/bursary/providers/:id` | Public | None | — | `{ provider }` (public fields only unless caller is that provider's admin) |
| PATCH | `/api/bursary/providers/:id` | Tenant Admin | None | Partial `bursary_providers` fields | `200 { provider }` |
| POST | `/api/bursary/providers/:id/modules` | Tenant Admin | None | Same as §3.1 modules body | `200 { activated, billingChange }` |
| GET | `/api/bursary/providers/:id/modules` | Tenant Admin | MOD_CORE | — | `{ modules: BursaryModuleConfig[] }` |
| GET | `/api/bursary/providers/:id/dashboard` | Tenant Admin | MOD_CORE | — | `{ summary: {...} }` |
| GET | `/api/bursary/providers/:id/analytics` | Tenant Admin | MOD_IMPACT_ANALYTICS | — | `{ analytics: {...} }` |

### 3.3 Fund CRUD

| Method | Path | Auth | Module Check | Request Body | Response |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| POST | `/api/bursary/funds` | Tenant Admin | MOD_CORE | `bursary_funds` insertable fields | `201 { fund }` |
| GET | `/api/bursary/funds` | Public | None | Query: `county`, `study_level`, `fund_type` | `{ funds: BursaryFund[] }` — tenant-scoped if `req.tenantId` set, cross-tenant open-funds list on `app.elimux.ke`/discovery portal otherwise |
| GET | `/api/bursary/funds/:id` | Public | None | — | `{ fund }` |
| PATCH | `/api/bursary/funds/:id` | Tenant Admin | MOD_CORE | Partial fields | `200 { fund }` |
| DELETE | `/api/bursary/funds/:id` | Tenant Admin | MOD_CORE | — | `204` (soft: sets `status='cancelled'`, never a hard delete — matches the disbursement ledger's immutability posture) |
| POST | `/api/bursary/funds/:id/duplicate` | Tenant Admin | MOD_CORE | — | `201 { fund }` |
| GET | `/api/bursary/funds/:id/applications` | Tenant Admin | MOD_CORE | Query: `status`, pagination | `{ applications: [], total }` |

## 4. Frontend Architecture

### 4.1 Next.js App Router Structure

Grounded against the real `elimux-frontend/src/app/` layout (top-level route groups already there: `about/`, `account/`, `admin/`, `advertiser/`, `applications/`, `dashboard/`, `institution/`, `internships/`, `partner/`, etc. — no existing `bursary/` or `tenant/` route yet, confirmed via directory listing, zero naming collision):

```
src/app/
  bursary/
    layout.tsx              — wraps children in TenantProvider (§4.2); reads
                               x-tenant-slug (set by middleware.ts, §5) or falls
                               back to the neutral discovery experience
    page.tsx                — cross-tenant fund discovery (mirrors /scholarships)
    [fundId]/page.tsx        — fund detail + apply CTA
    apply/[fundId]/page.tsx  — application wizard (§4.5)
    my-applications/page.tsx — student's bursary application list
    providers/
      register/page.tsx      — provider onboarding wizard (§4.5, §7.1)
      [slug]/page.tsx         — public provider transparency page (§3.12)
    admin/
      layout.tsx              — tenant-admin shell, gated by user_tenant_roles
      dashboard/page.tsx
      funds/page.tsx
      funds/new/page.tsx
      applications/page.tsx    — review queue, sorted by AI score
      applications/[id]/page.tsx
      disbursements/page.tsx
      branding/page.tsx        — white-label setup wizard (§7.1)
      modules/page.tsx         — module activation UI
      fraud/page.tsx           — fraud alert dashboard (module-gated)
    school/
      layout.tsx               — institution-admin shell
      students/page.tsx        — needy-student registry (§4.5)
      applications/page.tsx
  middleware.ts (root-level, extended) — adds tenant-slug header injection
```

Subdomain-served tenant portals (`slug.bursary.elimux.ke`) render the **same** `src/app/bursary/*` tree — the tenant is resolved from the Host header, not from a separate codebase or a separate Next.js project. This matches the v2 blueprint's principle ("business logic identical whether 1 tenant or 1000") and avoids the maintenance cost of parallel route trees.

### 4.2 Tenant Context Provider

`src/context/TenantContext.tsx` (new, sibling to the existing `AuthContext.tsx`) — structural description, not implementation:

- On mount, resolves the tenant slug from the `x-tenant-slug` request header (set at the edge by `middleware.ts`, §5.1) rather than re-parsing `window.location.host` client-side — avoids a layout flash on first paint for subdomain-served tenants.
- Fetches `GET /api/tenants/:slug/branding` once, caches in a `TenantProvider` React context (`useTenant()` hook, same naming convention as the existing `useAuth()`/`useAuthContext()` pair).
- On resolve, injects CSS custom properties (`--tenant-primary`, `--tenant-secondary`, `--tenant-font`) onto `document.documentElement`, sets `document.title`, and swaps the favicon `<link>` — see §7.
- On fetch failure (unknown slug, network error), falls back to ElimuX default branding rather than blocking render — matches the source blueprint's `.catch(() => setTenant(null))` behavior, described here as "fail open to default branding, never fail closed on the whole page."

### 4.3 Module Gating (hide UI if module not active)

`useModule(moduleId)` hook (new, `src/hooks/useModule.ts`): reads `activeModules` off the already-resolved `useTenant()` context (no extra network round-trip — the branding fetch in §4.2 also returns `activeModules`). Returns a boolean. Used to conditionally render admin-dashboard panels (§4.1's `fraud/page.tsx`, allocation-suggestion panels, etc.) and to short-circuit navigation links to gated features before the user even clicks into a 403.

### 4.4 Shared Components with ElimuX

Reused as-is, no fork: `AuthContext`/`useAuthContext` (root `layout.tsx` already wraps the whole app — Bursary Engine pages sit inside that same provider tree, so `useAuthContext()` works unchanged in `bursary/*` pages), `OfflineIndicator` (already wired into root layout since an earlier cycle), the PWA `BackgroundSyncManager`/`useBackgroundSync` pair (extended, not replaced — see §8), and the base `lib/api.ts` request client (new bursary-specific functions added to the same file, same `x-admin-key`/Bearer-token injection pattern already used for every other domain).

**Known hazard to avoid repeating:** per the documented `getSession()` deadlock history (Web Locks API contention when a component calls `supabase.auth.getSession()` directly instead of consuming `AuthProvider`'s already-resolved session), `TenantContext` must never call Supabase auth methods itself — tenant resolution is branding/module data only, entirely separate from auth state.

### 4.5 New Components

- `BursaryFundCard`, `BursaryFundFilters` — discovery (mirrors `ScholarshipCard` patterns already in the codebase)
- `ApplicationWizard` — multi-step form (eligibility preview → personal/academic/residence/household info → document upload → guardian consent if under 18 → review → submit), each step persisted to `bursary_applicants`/IndexedDB as the student progresses (not held only in React state, so a tab close doesn't lose progress)
- `DocumentUploader` — camera capture + gallery picker, shows forensics status per document (pending/verified/review/rejected) with the risk-score-to-color mapping from §9.1
- `StatusTracker` — visual pipeline (`submitted → document_check → institution_verify → govt_verify → provider_review → approved/rejected`), reads `bursary_applications.status`
- `ProviderDashboard` shell + panels: `ApplicationInbox` (sorted by `eligibility_score`), `DisbursementPanel`, `AIAllocationSuggestion` (module-gated), `FraudAlertPanel` (module-gated)
- `AdminFraudPanel` (super-admin only, cross-tenant — lives under the *existing* `/admin` tree, not `/bursary/admin`, since fraud registry access is platform-level per §2.11's RLS policy, not tenant-level)
- `BrandingWizard` — logo upload, color picker, font selector, contact/legal-pages form, live preview iframe (§7.1)
- `TenantChatAdvisor` — chat widget, module-gated on `MOD_AI_ADVISOR`, reuses whatever LLM-provider abstraction the existing AI routes already use (`AI_FALLBACK_ORDER`/`AI_MODE` env vars already exist per the live env var list — new prompts, not a new provider integration)

## 5. Tenant Resolution Implementation

*Pseudocode only, per the Risk constraint — the source blueprint's TypeScript is not reproduced verbatim.*

### 5.1 Edge: `middleware.ts` (Next.js, extended)

```
function middleware(request):
    host = request.headers['host']
    if host is one of the shared hosts (app.elimux.ke, admin.elimux.ke, api.elimux.ke):
        continue without a tenant header
    else if host has >= 3 dot-separated labels and label[0] != 'www':
        set request header x-tenant-slug = label[0]
    // custom-domain resolution (tenant_domains lookup) is NOT done here —
    // edge runtime has no direct Postgres access; custom domains resolve
    // server-side in resolveTenant (§5.2) instead, and the edge middleware
    // just passes the raw Host through unmodified in that case
    return next(request with headers)
```

### 5.2 Backend: `resolveTenant()` middleware (Express, mounted once ahead of the `/api/bursary` router)

```
function resolveTenant(req, res, next):
    host = req.headers['host']

    if host in SHARED_HOSTS:
        req.tenantId = null
        return next()

    customTenant = query tenant_domains WHERE domain = host AND verified = true AND status = 'active'
    if customTenant found:
        tenant = query tenants WHERE id = customTenant.tenant_id AND status = 'active'
        if tenant found:
            req.tenant = tenant; req.tenantId = tenant.id
            return next()

    slug = extractSubdomainLabel(host)  // mirrors §5.1's edge logic, re-derived
                                          // server-side since Express doesn't see
                                          // the x-tenant-slug header on direct
                                          // (non-proxied) API calls
    if slug present:
        tenant = query tenants WHERE slug = slug AND status = 'active'
        if tenant found:
            req.tenant = tenant; req.tenantId = tenant.id
            return next()

    headerTenantId = req.headers['x-tenant-id']  // mobile / API-client fallback
    if headerTenantId present:
        tenant = query tenants WHERE id = headerTenantId AND status = 'active'
        if tenant found:
            req.tenant = tenant; req.tenantId = tenant.id
            return next()

    // Nothing resolved
    if req.path starts with '/api/bursary/provider/' or '/api/bursary/admin/':
        return 404 { error: 'Tenant not found' }

    req.tenantId = null
    return next()
```

### 5.3 Custom Domain Resolution (detail)

Exact match against `tenant_domains.domain`, gated on both `verified = true` and `status = 'active'` (two separate flags deliberately — a domain can be DNS-verified but administratively suspended, e.g. during a billing dispute, without losing its verification record). No wildcard/CNAME pattern matching happens in application code; Vercel's own domain-add API (§7.2, Appendix C of the source blueprint) handles the actual DNS/SSL mechanics, this table just tracks which tenant a given exact hostname maps to.

### 5.4 Fallback to `x-tenant-id` Header

Exists specifically for API clients that can't rely on subdomain routing — a future mobile app, or a server-to-server integration (e.g. a government system polling `GET /api/bursary/gov/verifications/pending`). Lowest-priority resolution path: custom domain and subdomain both take precedence when present, so a browser request can never be spoofed into a different tenant via a stray header while a legitimate Host-based resolution also matches.

### 5.5 Setting Postgres `app.current_tenant_id` for RLS

Per v2 Appendix A, application code calls the `set_tenant_context(tenant_id)` RPC (a `SECURITY DEFINER` function wrapping `set_config('app.current_tenant_id', tenant_id::text, true)`, `true` = transaction-local, not session-global — critical on a pooled connection so one request's tenant context can never leak into the next request reusing the same pooled connection) immediately after `resolveTenant` succeeds, before any tenant-scoped query runs in that request. This is *defense in depth* — the backend's service-role client bypasses RLS entirely and its explicit `.eq('tenant_id', ...)` filters (§1.2 step 5) are what actually enforce isolation in every request today; `app.current_tenant_id` only matters for the RLS policies to do anything at all for a hypothetical future direct-from-browser Supabase client.

### 5.6 Error Handling: 404 vs. null-tenant fallthrough

Two distinct failure modes, not one: an *unresolvable* tenant on a tenant-required path (`/provider/`, `/admin/`) is a hard 404 (§5.2) — the caller asked for a specific tenant's private area and none exists. An unresolvable tenant on any other path (public discovery, `app.elimux.ke`) is *not* an error — `req.tenantId = null` and the request proceeds as a cross-tenant view. Conflating these (404-ing everything without a tenant) would break the entire cross-tenant discovery portal described in v2 §2.2's `app.elimux.ke` row.

### 6.2 `requireModule()` Middleware Factory — Pseudocode

```
function requireModule(moduleId):
    return function(req, res, next):
        if req.tenant is undefined:
            return 403 { error: 'Tenant context required' }
        if moduleId not in req.tenant.activeModules:
            return 403 { error: 'Module not activated', module: moduleId, upgrade_url: 'https://elimux.ke/pricing' }
        next()
```

Applied per-route (`router.post('/allocate-suggest', requireUser, requireModule('MOD_AI_ALLOCATION'), handler)`), never globally — mirrors exactly how the existing `adminRateLimiter`/`adminAuth` pair is already composed per-route in this backend (Cycle 006/007 pattern), not mounted as blanket middleware.

### 6.3 Per-Tenant Activation Check

`req.tenant.activeModules` (denormalized `text[]` on `tenants`, §2.1) is what `requireModule` reads — a single array-membership check, no extra query per gated request. `bursary_module_configs` (§2.12) holds the richer per-module `settings`/`usage_metrics`, read only by handlers that need it (e.g. `MOD_AI_ALLOCATION`'s equity-constraint settings), not by the gate itself. Activating/deactivating a module (`POST /api/tenants/:id/modules`, §3.1) writes both: updates `tenants.active_modules` (what the gate reads) and upserts the corresponding `bursary_module_configs` row (what handlers read for settings) — application code must keep these two in sync, since Postgres has no cross-table constraint that could enforce it automatically for a `text[]` vs. a separate settings table.

### 6.4 Module Settings Injection into Requests

For handlers that need settings beyond the boolean gate (e.g. `MOD_AI_ALLOCATION`'s `equity_constraints`), `requireModule` optionally attaches `req.moduleSettings = tenant.module_settings[moduleId]` after the activation check passes, so the handler doesn't issue its own follow-up query in the common case (settings already came back with the tenant row §5.2 fetched).

### 6.5 Frontend Module Gating: `useModule()` Hook

Covered in §4.3 — reads from the already-fetched `TenantContext`, no separate network call.

## 7. White-Label Implementation

### 7.1 Dynamic CSS Variable Injection

On tenant resolution (§4.2), `TenantProvider` sets `--tenant-primary`, `--tenant-secondary`, `--tenant-font` as inline custom properties on `document.documentElement`. Tailwind config (or component-level CSS) references these via `var(--tenant-primary, <ElimuX default>)` — the fallback value means an unbranded/default tenant (or a page rendered before the branding fetch resolves) never shows an unstyled flash, it just shows ElimuX's own palette until the tenant's colors land.

### 7.2 Meta Tag Generation Per Tenant

`document.title` and the `<meta name="description">` tag are updated client-side on resolution for SPA-navigated pages; for the initial SSR/SSG response (search-engine-visible), the `bursary/layout.tsx` Server Component reads `tenant_branding` server-side (via the same `x-tenant-slug` header §5.1 sets) and renders `generateMetadata()` per Next.js App Router convention — so a crawler hitting `nairobi-county.bursary.elimux.ke` directly sees Nairobi County's `meta_title`/`meta_description`/`og_image_url` in the initial HTML, not just after client-side hydration.

### 7.3 Favicon Swap

Client-side `<link rel="icon">` href swap on tenant resolution, same mechanism as the source blueprint. Sourced from `tenant_branding.favicon_url`, auto-generated server-side from the uploaded logo during onboarding (§7.1's wizard step 1) rather than requiring a separate favicon upload.

### 7.4 Email Template Customization

Handlebars or MJML, tenant variables (`{{provider_name}}`, `{{amount}}`, etc.) substituted at send time. Reuses the existing `lib/email.ts`/Resend integration (`RESEND_API_KEY` already in the live env var list) — new template functions added alongside the existing `scholarshipAwardedEmailHtml`/`applicationApprovedEmailHtml` pair, named distinctly (`bursaryApprovedEmailHtml`, etc.) to avoid the exact near-identical-name collision risk this codebase has already been bitten by once (`applicationApprovedEmailHtml` vs. `scholarshipAwardedEmailHtml` — different domains, easy to grab the wrong one). **Flag:** `elimux.ke` is not yet verified on Resend account-wide as of the last confirmed check — every transactional bursary email (approval, disbursement, document-verified) would 403 the same way existing scholarship-review emails currently do, until that's resolved. Not a Bursary-Engine-specific blocker, but it blocks the entire email leg of Phase 1 regardless.

### 7.5 SMS Template Customization

Full-text override per tenant, 160-char cap enforced at save time (not just at send time, so a tenant admin gets the error immediately in the branding UI rather than a silent truncation later). Provider needs confirming — no SMS provider (Twilio/Africa's Talking) integration exists in the live backend today; v1 §14 Phase 1 deliverables list "SMS notifications (Twilio/Africa's Talking)" as new work, not a reuse of existing infrastructure.

### 7.6 Public Page Generation Per Tenant

`GET /api/bursary/public/:providerSlug` (§3.12) backs `app/bursary/providers/[slug]/page.tsx` (§4.1) — server-rendered, tenant-branded (colors/logo via the same `generateMetadata`/CSS-variable mechanism), showing the stats/breakdowns/disbursement-table/impact-map described in v1 §13.1, gated per-field on that tenant's own `tenant_branding.show_recipient_names`/`show_amounts`/`show_aggregate_only` flags.

## 9. Security & Compliance

### 9.1 RLS Policy Patterns for Tenant Isolation

Every tenant-scoped table in §2 follows the same three-policy shape (public-read-if-applicable, tenant-admin-manage-own via `user_tenant_roles`, and — where relevant — the requesting user's-own-record read). The single deliberate exception is `bursary_fraud_registry` (§2.11), which has **no** tenant-scoped policy at all — cross-tenant fraud defense requires a provider to never see another provider's flagged identifiers, so it's platform-`super_admin`-only, full stop. `bursary_disbursements` (§2.10) is the other deliberate exception in the other direction — no `UPDATE`/`DELETE` policy exists for *any* role, enforcing the immutable-ledger design at the database layer rather than trusting application code alone not to mutate a settled disbursement.

### 9.2 Cross-Tenant Fraud Registry (Hashed Identifiers Only)

Per v1 §12.4: `national_id_hash`/`phone_hash`/`email_hash`/`device_fingerprint` are salted SHA-256 — raw PII is never written to `bursary_fraud_registry.identifiers`, only into the tenant-scoped `bursary_applicants.personal_info` (itself RLS-protected to the owning student + that tenant's reviewers). New applications are checked against the registry by re-hashing the same fields with the same salt and comparing — a false-positive risk if the salt or hash function ever changes without a registry-wide re-hash migration, worth flagging as an operational constraint once this moves to implementation, not solved by this document alone.

### 9.3 Data Minimization Per Tenant

Application data collection matches v1's per-fund `required_documents`/`eligibility_rules` — a tenant only sees the fields relevant to funds it operates, enforced by the same RLS policies as §9.1 (a fund's `eligibility_rules` are that fund's own `bursary_funds` row; a provider's dashboard queries never join across tenants for anything but the intentionally cross-tenant fraud registry).

### 9.4 Kenya Data Protection Act 2019 / GDPR Alignment

Directly reusing v1 §16.1's compliance mapping (already correct and Kenya-specific, not re-derived here), with one concrete correction against live code: the source blueprint says GDPR export/delete are "extended to include bursary data" as if that's a future step — it actually needs to be, because `/api/user/export-data` (shipped Cycle 012) and `/api/user/delete-account` (shipped Cycle 014) **already exist and run today** for the scholarship platform. When Bursary Engine ships, both routes need real additions (not just documentation): `export-data` must add `bursary_applicants`/`bursary_applications`/`bursary_documents`/`bursary_disbursements` (matched by `user_id`, same as every other table those routes already handle) to its response, and `delete-account` needs the same anonymize-vs-hard-delete policy decision Cycle 014 already had to make for scholarship data (documents and disbursements are financial/audit records — likely anonymize, not delete, matching how Cycle 014 anonymized `scholarship_messages` rather than deleting them) — an open design question, not resolved here, but the two routes that need touching are named precisely, not "somewhere in the backend."

### 9.5 Audit Logging Strategy

`bursary_audit_logs` (§2.15) — every state-changing action on `bursary_applications`/`bursary_disbursements`/`tenants`/`user_tenant_roles` writes a row (actor, action, before/after state, IP via `x-forwarded-for` — Railway strips the real client IP on `req.ip`, a fix already applied elsewhere in this backend, e.g. `reviews.ts`, that must be replicated here rather than re-discovered). `bursary_applications.audit_trail` (a `jsonb[]` column on the row itself, per v1 §3.4) remains for a fast "show this application's history" read without a join; `bursary_audit_logs` is the durable, cross-entity, admin-queryable log — the two are complementary, not duplicates.

### 9.6 Secrets Management (Env Vars Per Module)

No *new* secret-management mechanism needed — reuses the existing Railway env-var pattern (`ADMIN_KEY`, `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY`, etc., already gated per the existing `supabaseConfigOk` startup guard that logs loudly rather than silently proceeding on a misconfigured key). Module-specific secrets that will actually be new: `MPESA_PASSKEY`/`MPESA_SHORTCODE`/`MPESA_CALLBACK_URL` (currently unset, blocking §3.10/§8's M-Pesa disbursement regardless of module activation state), an SMS provider key (Twilio or Africa's Talking, not yet chosen), and — only if `MOD_THIRD_PARTY_VERIFY` is ever activated by a tenant — a Smile ID/Onfido API key, which given it's Phase 3 (§10) is out of scope for anything before then.

## 10. Implementation Phases

Combining v2's launch-strategy framing (§20, "launch with 1 provider, tenant-aware from day one") with v1's more granular per-phase deliverable list, plus the Task 2-required per-phase breakdown (tables / endpoints / pages / modules / testing):

### Phase 1: Foundation (Weeks 1–4) — LAUNCH WITH 1 PROVIDER

**Goal:** one provider (per the instruction's Background, a real founder-selected tenant) live with full branding, before any second tenant is onboarded.

- **Tables:** `tenants`, `tenant_domains`, `tenant_branding`, `user_tenant_roles`, `bursary_providers`, `bursary_funds`, `bursary_applicants`, `bursary_applications`, `bursary_documents`, `bursary_disbursements`, `bursary_module_configs`, `bursary_audit_logs` (§2.1–2.9, 2.12, 2.15 — everything except the two later-phase tables below)
- **Endpoints:** §3.1 (tenant mgmt), §3.2 (provider onboarding), §3.3 (fund CRUD), §3.4 (student self-service), §3.5 (school-mediated), §3.7 (institution verification), §3.10's M-Pesa + external disbursement rows only (bank transfer is Phase 2), §3.14 (offline sync)
- **Frontend pages:** all of §4.1 except nothing deferred — Phase 1 needs the full route tree, since even Phase-1-only modules touch every page (admin dashboard, branding wizard, application wizard, document uploader, status tracker)
- **Modules active:** every module marked "On" in §6.1's table — `MOD_CORE`, `MOD_DISBURSE_MPESA`, `MOD_DISBURSE_EXTERNAL`, `MOD_VERIFY_INSTITUTION`, `MOD_SCHOOL_MEDIATED`, `MOD_GUARDIAN_CONSENT`, `MOD_OFFLINE_QUEUE`, plus rule-based `MOD_AI_ELIGIBILITY` and basic `MOD_AI_FORENSICS`/`MOD_AI_FRAUD` (ML/advanced versions are Phase 2, per v1's split)
- **Real prerequisites this phase depends on, not yet resolved (see §8):** M-Pesa credentials (`MPESA_PASSKEY`/`SHORTCODE`/`CALLBACK_URL`) and an SMS provider decision — both block real disbursement/notification even after all code above ships.
- **Testing milestones:** one tenant end-to-end (register → verify → create fund → student applies → guardian consent if applicable → document forensics → institution verify → provider approves → M-Pesa disburses → student receives SMS receipt → public transparency page shows aggregate stats); RLS isolation test (a second, test-only tenant created and confirmed to see zero rows of the first tenant's data before any real second provider onboards); GDPR export/delete extension (§9.4) verified against a real bursary applicant record.

### Phase 2: Intelligence (Weeks 5–8) — 5–10 PROVIDERS

- **Tables:** `tenant_billing` (§2.13) — first phase billing actually matters, since Free-tier providers from Phase 1 don't need it
- **Endpoints:** §3.6 (document forensics async analysis, advanced), §3.8 (government verification), §3.9 (AI allocation/review), §3.11 (all AI services), §3.10's bank-transfer rows, §3.1's custom-domain routes (`MOD_CUSTOM_DOMAIN`)
- **Frontend pages:** `admin/fraud/page.tsx` panel goes live (module-gated, was hidden all of Phase 1), `AIAllocationSuggestion` panel, appeals UI, renewal application flow
- **Modules activated:** `MOD_AI_ALLOCATION`, `MOD_AI_RENEWAL`, `MOD_AI_ADVISOR`, `MOD_DISBURSE_BANK`, `MOD_VERIFY_GOVT`, `MOD_CUSTOM_DOMAIN`, ML-upgraded `MOD_AI_ELIGIBILITY`, advanced `MOD_AI_FORENSICS`/`MOD_AI_FRAUD`
- **Testing milestones:** MILP allocation solve on a realistic multi-hundred-applicant fund, verified against the equity constraints in v1 §5.4; multi-tenant billing correctness (two tenants on different plans, usage metering doesn't cross-contaminate); custom domain DNS+SSL flow end-to-end on one real provider's own domain.

### Phase 3: Scale & Compliance (Weeks 9–12) — 20–50 PROVIDERS

- **Tables:** none new — this phase is analytics/compliance features on top of existing tables (e.g. `bursary_applicants.academic_info`/`residence_info` extended for multi-country fields, via `ALTER TABLE`, not a new table)
- **Endpoints:** `MOD_THIRD_PARTY_VERIFY` hooks into §3.6's forensics pipeline, `MOD_IMPACT_ANALYTICS` extends §3.2's provider analytics endpoint, `MOD_TRANSPARENCY_AUDIT` extends §3.12
- **Frontend pages:** advanced analytics dashboard, mentorship matching interface
- **Modules activated:** `MOD_THIRD_PARTY_VERIFY`, `MOD_MENTORSHIP`, `MOD_IMPACT_ANALYTICS`, `MOD_TRANSPARENCY_AUDIT`
- **Testing milestones:** multi-currency disbursement correctness (a second currency's rounding/precision, not just a label swap); third-party verification hook failure-mode test (Smile ID/Onfido timeout must degrade to internal-score-only, never block the pipeline).

### Phase 4: Ecosystem (Weeks 13–16) — 100+ PROVIDERS

- **Tables:** none new to this blueprint's scope — alumni giving/crowdfunding/USSD each imply their own schema, explicitly out of scope for this Instruction 015 (which is architecture for the Phase-1-through-3 core, not a full spec for Phase 4's ecosystem features)
- **Modules activated:** `MOD_ALUMNI_GIVING`, `MOD_USSD`
- **Testing milestones:** deferred — Phase 4 needs its own blueprint cycle once Phases 1–3 are live and real usage data exists to design against, rather than speculatively specced now.

## 11. Performance & Scaling

### 11.1 Database Indexing Strategy

Every FK column used in an RLS policy or a hot-path filter has an explicit `CREATE INDEX` in §2 (not left to Postgres's automatic FK-backing, which doesn't always create one) — `tenant_id` on every tenant-scoped table (the single most common filter, per §1.2 step 5), `status`/`application_status` where funds/applications are frequently filtered by state, `perceptual_hash`/`file_hash` on `bursary_documents` for duplicate-detection lookups (§9.2), a GIN index on `bursary_fraud_registry.identifiers` (jsonb containment queries for hash matching, not a plain btree).

### 11.2 Query Optimization for Tenant-Scoped Data

The `.eq('tenant_id', ...)` filter (§1.2) should be the **first** predicate in every tenant-scoped query specifically because `idx_*_tenant` indexes exist — Postgres's planner uses that index to narrow the row set before applying any other filter, matching the existing codebase's pattern of filtering by the most selective indexed column first (e.g. `scholarship_applications` queries already filter by `student_id` first for the same reason).

### 11.3 CDN Configuration for Tenant Assets

Logos/branding images served from the existing Supabase Storage `logos`-bucket-equivalent (public bucket, CDN-fronted by Supabase's own edge network) — no separate CDN integration needed, matching how institution logos already work today. `custom_css` (§2.3, a `text` column) is small enough to inline in the SSR'd `<head>` rather than needing its own asset pipeline.

### 11.4 Rate Limiting Per Tenant

Reuses the existing `express-rate-limit` dependency (already in `elimux-backend/package.json`, already wired to admin routes since Cycle 006/007 — not a new library to add). New tenant-scoped limiter keyed on `req.tenantId` (not IP, which the existing admin limiter uses) for endpoints like `POST /api/bursary/applications` (prevent one tenant's traffic spike from starving another tenant's rate budget on a shared service) and a *per-student* limiter on `POST /api/bursary/ai/chat-advisor` (the 50 msg/hour cap from v1 §5.6).

### 11.5 Caching Strategy

Tenant branding/modules (§4.2's fetch) is the highest-value cache target — read on every page load, changes rarely. Redis is not currently part of the stack (unverified in this cycle; no Redis client found in `elimux-backend/package.json` during grounding checks) — Railway in-memory caching (a simple TTL map inside the single Express process) is the pragmatic Phase 1 choice, with a note that it stops being safe the moment the backend scales beyond one Railway instance (cache inconsistency across instances) — Redis becomes a real requirement at that point, not before.

### 11.6 File Upload Optimization

Matches the existing `scholarship-documents` pattern exactly: 5MB cap (`documentUpload.ts`'s `MAX_SIZE_MB`, mirrored in §2.9's bucket config), same `application/pdf`/`image/jpeg`/`image/png` allow-list. Virus-scan hooks are new work (not present in the existing upload path either) — flagged as a genuine Phase 1 gap if document uploads for a government-funded program need it for compliance, not assumed to already exist anywhere in this stack.

## 12. Deployment & DevOps

### 12.1 Vercel Wildcard Domain Configuration

Per the instruction's Background, `bursary.elimux.ke` is already added to the Vercel project and generating SSL. What still needs configuring for the wildcard pattern (`*.bursary.elimux.ke`) is the Vercel project's Domains setting adding the wildcard entry itself (Vercel auto-provisions SSL for wildcard domains, per v2 Appendix B) — this is a dashboard/API action, not a code change, and is not verified as done in this cycle (docs-only, per the Risk constraint).

### 12.2 Railway Service Configuration

No new Railway service — new routes on the existing `elimux-backend` service (§8). Railway does not support wildcard subdomains directly (per v2 Appendix B), which is why the recommended path is Cloudflare-proxied DNS in front of both Vercel and Railway: `*.bursary.elimux.ke`/`app.elimux.ke`/`admin.elimux.ke` → `cname.vercel-dns.com`, `api.elimux.ke` → Railway, with a Page Rule bypassing cache on `api.elimux.ke/api/*` (APIs should never be edge-cached) and caching static assets on the `*.bursary.elimux.ke` subdomains.

### 12.3 Supabase Migration Strategy

Flat numbered files in `elimux-sql/` (verified convention, §2's header note) — the 15 `CREATE TABLE` statements in §2 become `44_bursary_tenants.sql` through roughly `58_...sql` when implementation starts (sequential, one concern per file, matching how existing migrations are split — e.g. `41_scholarship_documents_bucket.sql` is bucket-only, not bundled with unrelated schema changes). Every file pasted by hand into the Supabase Dashboard SQL editor — there is no migration runner in this project (verified: no `migrations/` folder, no `supabase db push` usage found in either repo) — so each file must be re-verified against the live schema immediately before pasting, not assumed to apply cleanly from this document alone.
